# Retrospective: PR #12784

## Worked
Fresh native Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral scope. Security triage preceded launch and runtime. Independent reports distinguished removal of the CLI override from unverified application behavior. The small source comparison makes that boundary visible. A focused documentation correction was retained rather than inflating an untested security hypothesis into a confirmed defect.

## Deviations and remediation
- Opus read 72 policy lines once, exceeding the 60-line cap. Public policy text only, retained native history. Keep all Claude policy chunks at 60 or fewer lines.
- Nested upstream test writes lacked per-target resolved assertions and upstream cleanup discarded internal logs. Background routing observed readiness without recording completion/exit. Preserve the sealed runs and audit-addendum.md. Do not claim full guard coverage or native behavior. Future fixtures must inventory actual callee targets, retain internal streams/status before cleanup, and require explicit completion for background producers. Narrow observed test output and direct source comparison independently support this draft.
- Coordinator read one saved final before the second finished, then reread both after completion. No peer disclosure or premature synthesis occurred. Future collection must wait for both finals before reading either.
- The assignment-owned repository is blobless. GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 correctly rejected history content queries lacking blobs; errors remain retained. Materialize needed history explicitly before read-only investigation rather than relying on implicit fetches.

## Limits and stopping
Native 1Password behavior needs resources and permissions absent here. Additional synthetic fixtures could not establish it, so neither reviewer claimed to do so. No generic requests for more tests were added. No confirmed toolkit/desktop bug arose. No resources were borrowed, and no browser was opened.

## Cleanup
Both review.py runs completed and their private namespaces ended. No lingering owned test process or private runtime home remains. Source/evidence and historical sessions retained. Coordinator does not reset itself or choose subsequent work.

**Verified:** At `1933655`, the explicit `1password --lock` call is removed while the lock-screen request, keyboard-layout reset and screensaver shutdown sequence remain unchanged. No runtime regression was confirmed in the reviewed scope; one documentation correction remains.

Source comparison:

```text
Before: Omarchy lock -> explicit 1Password CLI lock
After:  Omarchy lock -> no explicit 1Password CLI lock
                       native app response not verified
```

**Documentation correction:** [The lock-screen manual](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/1933655cc20bb37d7c3b8ef086593ee8a342e1fa/manual/13-toggles-idle-screensaver.md#L99) still says the shortcut “locks 1Password on the way out” whenever it is running. **Suggested change:** remove that unconditional promise and explain that Omarchy no longer explicitly locks 1Password.

**Native behavior remains unverified:** The enabled-preference case depends on 1Password detecting this desktop's lock. The source requests Quickshell's Wayland session lock, and the linked support article documents the preference without establishing that integration. These checks therefore do not establish the PR's claim that 1Password still locks when the preference is enabled, nor demonstrate that it fails.

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection, per-file shell syntax checks and the focused shell test. The new assertion passed on the PR and rejected the original lock script. No native 1Password, compositor, suspend or credential-integration behavior was tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical reviews, followed by verification against source and targeted evidence.
